document_title: Brunswick County Chancery Cause 1811-003, Patsey J. Brock v. Adin Linch & wife: Lot No. 2 of the division of the Negroes of the estate of Judith Jones dec'd
collection_identifier: Brunswick County (Va.) Chancery Causes, Index No. 1811-003, Box 016, image 0013 (Lot No. 2); 0005 (decree, Aug. Term 1810); 0007 (report, 23 Mar 1811); 0015-0016 (Lot No. 1)
exact_relevant_transcription: Lott No 2. Adin Linch: Butcher £110.0.0; Solomon 90.0.0; Joe 70.0.0; Violet 55.0.0; Woodley 15.0.0; Lucey 95.0.0; German 18.0.0; Nelley 50.0.0; [total] £503.0.0. Report: 'We the undersigned commissioners ... have this day proceeded to make the division of the Estate of Judith Jones dec'd ... Nos 1 & 2 will fully discover & exhibit the division of the Negroes ... Given under our hands this 23d day of March Eighteen hundred & eleven. Willie Harrison, Edward Dromgoole, Claiborne House, Commissioners'
evidence_supporting_identification: Enslaved person named Woodley in Brunswick County, Va., in 1811; low valuation (£15, with German £18) consistent with a young child, which fits a birth c.1804-1809; Edward Dromgoole was a court-appointed commissioner of the division (documented Dromgoole link to this Woodley, as commissioner only); 'Anthony' (name of a son in the 1870 household) is in Lot No. 1
evidence_contradicting_identification: Woodley is a given name only; at least 8 other Virginia chancery suits index an enslaved 'Woodley'; no age, parentage or later movement recorded; the enslaver was Adin Linch, not a Dromgoole; no document yet links this Woodley to Louisiana

evidence_contradicting_identification: Absence is not proof of sale; the remaining 19 pages of the suit were not read and could mention Woodley
